tonight.headline: A 48-point lead with Daniels and Loveland still to play
body: Bad news first: Jonathan Taylor scored 6.7 on eight carries in a 42-7 loss — no injury, just a blowout — and the Colts, who traded Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, are now taking calls on him before the 10 November deadline. Five teams have checked in (Schultz via NBC). That is a Week 9 question, not tonight's.

Bloodsports lead Metcalf Gala 124.5 to 76.2 with Daniels (tonight, 19:20) and Loveland (Monday, 19:15) still to play; ESPN 99%. Daniels is good to go with no designation. The lineup as set is the projection lineup and nothing can change it except a Loveland inactive Monday, with no cover available.

case.label: Where it stands
case.body: Jacobs 23.2, Golden 20.9, Tuten 29.9, Jaguars D/ST 19.5, Wilson 14.3, Gay 10, Taylor 6.7 final. Two starters left.

case.label: Taylor's market
case.body: Colts "fielding calls but not actively shopping" (BVM 1 Nov); Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers have checked in (NBC 1 Nov). A trade moves his role either way; there is nothing to do until it happens.

worthALook.name: DeMario Douglas
worthALook.lead: A.J. Brown is OUT (ankle/knee, Patriots.com 31 Oct); ESPN and Football Nation name Douglas as the target to use.

case.label: The player
case.body: Brown downgraded to OUT on Saturday; three healthy receivers remain, Douglas in the slot (Patriots.com 31 Oct). 19.6 on 8 touches in Week 6 (archive).

case.label: Why not now
case.body: A one-week vacancy with no multi-week timeline, and he would be a fifth receiver behind Golden, Wilson, Pickens and Rice. A free agent — he costs no priority, so there is no reason to move before the role proves out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Brown reported multi-week and Douglas above 25% of targets Sunday, or Pickens ruled out for multiple weeks — then a free-agent add, Pitts the drop.

doNotChase.name: T.J. Hockenson
doNotChase.lead: Free, and still not needed: Loveland plays Monday.

case.label: The case for
case.body: Not on the Vikings' final report (PurplePTSD 31 Oct); Kyler Murray starts; Detroit allow the most tight-end points. He was the Sunday cover for Loveland's neck — a question Saturday's Bears report closed.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 11.3 against Pitts' 10.4 — 0.9, a coin flip. Adding him means dropping Pitts, added on 28 Oct; that seat changed hands inside seven days and nobody in it is ruled out (STRATEGY §3).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loveland's neck flaring up after Monday, or a multi-week injury to him — then Hockenson for Pitts is a real upgrade, made after Week 8.
